feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: The Rhine at Kaub, Germany dipped again, continuing an uneven recovery
entry.summary: Germany's main shipping gauge at Kaub read 11 centimetres at 6:30am on 16 October, down from 16 centimetres the previous day. — Sources: Pegelonline (Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung), direct gauge fetch, 16 October 2026

entry.title: Indonesia ruled out declaring its forest fires a national disaster and confirmed Malaysia's and Singapore's aid offers were not discussed
entry.summary: Indonesia's coordinating minister said the government remains capable of handling the fires without declaring a national disaster, directing resources toward protecting Tanjung Puting National Park. — Sources: Antara/asianews.network, 13 October 2026 · The Vibes, 13 October 2026

entry.title: Indonesia's fire-hotspot count fell for a second straight reading
entry.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Forestry recorded 11,037 hotspots nationally on 13 October, continuing a fall from the season's peak of 24,952 on 8 October and an interim reading of 20,818 on 12 October. — Sources: Ministry of Forestry/SiPongi, via databoks.katadata.co.id, 13 October 2026

entry.title: Haze-driven school closures in Johor, Malaysia affected more than 600,000 students
entry.summary: All schools and religious institutions across Johor state stayed closed from 10 to 16 October as the state's air quality readings held between 170 and 180 with no sustained improvement, a closure affecting 617,258 students across 1,198 schools. — Sources: The Star Malaysia, 10 October 2026 · New Straits Times, 10 October 2026

entry.title: Luxembourg will not set a binding workplace heat limit, unlike its neighbours
entry.summary: Luxembourg's labour minister told Parliament that existing risk-assessment rules already allow for the necessary protections, and declined to adopt a maximum workplace temperature, unlike France, Belgium and Spain. — Sources: Paperjam, 16 October 2026
